newsitem.title: USA: SGL Carbon shares suspended from U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon shares suspended from U.S. trade.

text.p: Shares in German carbon and graphite maker SGL Carbon AG were suspended from trade on Wall Street on Thursday pending an announcement, the New York Stock Exchange said.
Before the suspension, the U.S. shares had fallen 4-3/4 to 46. Earlier, the company's stock dropped more than 11 percent in German trade.
The declines came amid speculation that an SGL Carbon unit in the United States faced a legal battle over alleged price fixing. No one from the company was available for comment.

SGL Carbon's rival UCAR International Inc was also suspended earlier Thursday. UCAR said it had been served with a subpoena and related search warrant from a U.S. grand jury investigating alleged price fixing by producers of graphite electrodes. UCAR is the world's largest maker of graphite and carbon electrodes.
Trade in the shares was resumed later, the New York Stock Exchange said.
